question: Does transferring a prior center from other benchmarks improve over fixed Beta(1,1)?
fit: Within each training benchmark, average the full-response success rates of eligible subject groups equally. Average the four training benchmark means equally. Exclude all outcomes from the held-out benchmark. No model-name features or item-text predictor.
folds: Leave one complete benchmark out; shared model identities are allowed, as in the benchmark cold-start task.
primary_endpoint: Equal-pair Brier ALC on saved item splits, averaged over three acquisition seeds; also report equal-benchmark ALC and exact conditional expectations.
screening_rule: Continue to genuinely new public validation only if both equal-pair and equal-benchmark observed and expected ALC improve, at least four of five benchmarks improve in observed and expected ALC, and the equal-benchmark direction remains favorable when coding and BertaQA use guarded splits. This is a development screen, not automatic replacement of the submission.
leakage_check: Hash-check original data and saved trajectories. Exclude the complete target benchmark from fit. Audit normalized exact and 0.9-Jaccard cross-benchmark question overlap across eligible items, using BertaQA final user questions. Stop before comparison if cross-benchmark matches exist.
constraints: One fixed method; no center or strength grid search, no leaderboard queries, no API, no GPU, no new downloads.
limitations: All five benchmarks were inspected previously; this is adaptive development, not fresh confirmatory evidence.
Lexical checks do not exclude all semantic or document-level overlap.
Three acquisition seeds share pools and are not independent benchmark replications.
Saved full groups do not reproduce the hosted balancing and 1000-pair sampling cap.
The trained center assumes training success rates transfer to new benchmarks; domain shift may make this worse than 0.5.
